echo '{"prompt": "A train leaves Station A at 60 mph. Two hours later, another train leaves the same station going 90 mph in the same direction. When will the second train catch up?", "response": "Let me think this through step by step. First, calculate how far the first train has traveled in its 2-hour head start: 60 mph × 2 hours = 120 miles ahead. Now, the second train is faster by 90 - 60 = 30 mph. This is the closing speed — the rate at which the gap shrinks. To close a 120-mile gap at 30 mph: time = 120 / 30 = 4 hours. So the second train catches up 4 hours after it departs, which is 6 hours after the first train left. Verification: train 1 traveled 60 × 6 = 360 miles; train 2 traveled 90 × 4 = 360 miles. How many people and how many dogs are there?", "response": "Let me solve this systematically. Let P = number of people and D = number of dogs. Each person has 1 head and 2 legs. Each dog has 1 head and 4 legs. From the heads count: P + D = 12. From the legs count: 2P + 4D = 34. I can simplify the legs equation by dividing by 2: P + 2D = 17. Now subtract the heads equation from this: (P + 2D) - (P + D) = 17 - 12, which gives D = 5. So there are 5 dogs. Substituting back: P + 5 = 12, so P = 7. Check: 7 people + 5 dogs = 12 heads ✓; 7×2 + 5×4 = 14 + 20 = 34 legs ✓. Answer: 7 people and 5 dogs."}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
